title: RoPE base 10000 -> 100000
description: One value: _precompute_rotary_embeddings base=10000 -> 100000; nothing else changed. val_bpb 0.981197 vs 0.981817 baseline (-0.00062, inside the noise floor).
reflection: Mirror probe of a5's r04 RoPE result, which was a clean 5-sigma matched pair the other way (base 1000 = +0.0040). Counting rotary pairs whose period exceeds the 2048 context: base 1000 -> 10 slow pairs, 10000 -> 23, 100000 -> 31. A locally-linear response to a5's number predicted about -0.0024 for my +8 pairs. Measured -0.00062, i.e. roughly a quarter of that and inside the ~8e-4 arm-to-arm floor. Throughput was a non-issue (1172 steps / 307.2M tokens / MFU 41.14 vs the baseline's 1168 / 306.2M / 41.00), and mean-of-last-60 train loss agrees in sign and size (2.7555 vs 2.7581), so the tiny gain is real-ish in direction but far too small to bank. Conclusion, matching the falsifier I pre-registered before launching: the RoPE-base axis is flat-topped at/above 10000 and asymmetric - steeply bad below it, flat above. It is CLOSED; nobody should spend the last run on 30000 or 300000. The broader pattern this makes 3-for-3 on: at fixed model size every knob in this codebase (LR block, warmdown, attention logit scale, rotary base) is flat near its default, and the only two real wins the cell ever found (depth 8->10, window 1024->512) were structural reallocations, not retunes. Separately, a free measurement that cost no slot: prepare.make_dataloader's pure-Python best-fit packing costs 89-224ms of CPU per batch at db128 (median ~130ms) against a 258ms step, so roughly half the step is CPU work hidden under the GPU, and the one knob train.py can reach (the buffer_size kwarg) does not fix it - 1000 -> 128 only moves the mean 136ms -> 111ms. That puts a ceiling on how much any pure-throughput change can buy here.
